proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true admission lag is closer to 1 week (or varies within-season), a fixed 2-week delay can shift peaks late and under/over-shoot during rapid rise/decline periods.
proposals.rationale: Anchor on the dominant discovered template (SEIRS + delayed_I) while prioritizing a modest 2-week lag that aligns with hospitalization timing and has shown comparatively better rolling stability than 1-week in prior feedback.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May overfit timing to a particular held-out segment; can degrade on rolling splits if the effective lag is longer or changes over time, leading to premature peaks.
proposals.rationale: Include the prior best spec as a comparator within the recommended narrow delay band; maintains parsimony and tests whether the 1-week lag remains robust beyond a single validation window.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Higher split-to-split variability/instability in short series (31 train weeks); may introduce spurious persistence or heavy-tailed dynamics that mis-time peaks and inflate uncertainty.
proposals.rationale: Single fractional variant allowed by constraints: paired with the more stable 2-week delay to test whether fractional dynamics improve robustness for moderate peakiness/high scale without expanding mechanisms beyond the template knobs.
